detail.body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Scope: this is a host-dispatch microbenchmark, not an end-to-end throughput claim.**
> The numbers below are measured on the host build path, with per-call dispatch counts. Against a multi-millisecond decode step a
> change of this size sits inside run-to-run variation (~1% on a conc=1 arm), so
> **no measurable serving throughput improvement is claimed, and none should be
> inferred.** The value is removing host torch dispatches that serialize against the GPU on a path that is
> on the critical path at low concurrency. Details under "End-to-end (side note)".

## Summary

Two spots on the MLA attention metadata build spend more time in PyTorch
dispatch than in the work they do. Both operate on tensors that are already
host-side and hold one entry per request, and both run on **every** build,
between decode steps.

### 1. `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder._uniform_padded_mtp_qo_len`

Eight tensor dispatches — `sum()/item()`, a boolean-mask index, `numel()`,
`torch.all`, `eq`, `torch.nonzero`, `item()`, `torch.any` — to decide a single
integer. `qo_len` is derived from `query_start_loc_cpu`.

### 2. `MLACommonMetadataBuilder.build`, non-causal multi-token decode

A validation block using `torch.count_nonzero`, two `torch.all` calls and two
tensor-to-bool conversions (each lowering to `aten::is_nonzero`), purely to
raise a `ValueError` on a malformed query block.

Both now read the tensor out once and decide on Python ints.

## Results

Host cost, measured **without a GPU**. Both inputs are CPU tensors, so there is
no device work and no profiler involved in these numbers.

**`_uniform_padded_mtp_qo_len`**

| reqs | before | after | speedup | saved |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1.88 µs | 0.32 µs | **5.9×** | 1.56 µs |
| 2 | 17.62 µs | 0.53 µs | **33.6×** | 17.10 µs |
| 8 | 17.65 µs | 0.71 µs | **24.8×** | 16.94 µs |

**non-causal query-block validation**

| reqs | before | after | speedup | saved |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 11.88 µs | 0.84 µs | **14.1×** | 11.04 µs |
| 2 | 12.44 µs | 0.89 µs | **13.9×** | 11.55 µs |
| 8 | 12.58 µs | 1.20 µs | **10.5×** | 11.38 µs |

Combined at 2 requests: **30.06 µs → 1.42 µs, ~21×, 14 tensor dispatches
removed per build.**

The step from one request to two in the first table is the padded-CUDA-graph
case: with dummy rows present the function stops early-returning and runs the
full `nonzero`/`any` path, which is the shape a graph-captured decode hits.

## Why this path matters

On a Kimi-K3 conc=1 384K-context decode trace, all 8 GPUs are idle across the
metadata-build window between decode steps, so host time there is on the
critical path rather than overlapped. These two sites account for the
`count_nonzero`, `is_nonzero` and `eq`/`nonzero` operations visible in that
window.

## Correctness

No FLOPs change and no device work changes; both sites return small integers
and booleans.

- `_uniform_padded_mtp_qo_len`: **34067 cases, 0 mismatches** — exhaustive over
  every `qo_len` combination up to 4 requests × length 4 crossed with every
  plausible `num_decode_tokens`, plus 20000 randomised larger cases. Covers
  empty, all-zero, zero-interior, non-divisible totals, `uniform_qo_len <= 1`
  and trailing-zero inputs.
- non-causal validation: **21364 cases, 0 mismatches** — exhaustive over every
  query-length combination up to 5 requests × length 3, plus 20000 randomised
  cases, comparing all three returned predicates.

The `ValueError` text is unchanged: it now formats a list rather than calling
`.tolist()` on a tensor.

## Tests run

```
ruff check vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py \
           vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py
All checks passed!

ruff format --check <same two files>
2 files already formatted
```

Equivalence harnesses were run inside `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` on CPU; output is
the case counts quoted above.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs before writing this:

```
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "_uniform_padded_mtp_qo_len"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "rocm_aiter_mla host"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "non-causal MLA uniform query block"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "mla_attention count_nonzero"
```

Nearby open PRs (#57085, #57464, #54546, #58344) touch this area but none
addresses the host cost of these two functions.

## End-to-end (side note)

Deliberately last, and not the claim being made. End-to-end effect at this
operating point depends on how many metadata builds occur per step and on the
tuning of surrounding kernels, which is out of scope here. On our conc=1
Kimi-K3 configuration the expected effect is well under the run-to-run spread
we measure (~0.8%), so the function-level speedup above is the honest result.

---

AI assistance was used for this change (Claude Opus 5). The measurements were
run by the submitter on MI355X hardware, and every changed line was reviewed by
the submitter.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,104 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Differential test for the AITER MLA uniform-MTP padding decision.
+
+`_uniform_padded_mtp_qo_len` decides whether a full-CUDA-graph decode batch may
+synthesize dummy query rows. It used to reach that decision through eight tensor
+dispatches -- sum/item, boolean-mask index, all, eq, nonzero, item, any -- on a
+CPU tensor holding one entry per request. It now reads the tensor out once and
+decides on Python ints.
+
+That rewrite also **reordered** the checks: the `num_decode_tokens <= sum(...)`
+early-out moved below the divisibility and `uniform_qo_len <= 1` guards. Every
+one of those paths returns 0, so the result should be unchanged -- but "should
+be" is exactly the sort of claim worth checking exhaustively, so both
+implementations are carried here and compared over the whole small input space.
+
+Pure host arithmetic; no GPU required.
+"""
+
+import itertools
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.rocm_aiter_mla import AiterMLAMetadataBuilder
+
+
+def _reference(qo_len: torch.Tensor, max_qo_len: int, num_decode_tokens: int) -> int:
+    """The pre-#58381 implementation, verbatim."""
+    num_reqs = qo_len.numel()
+    if num_reqs == 0 or num_decode_tokens <= 0:
+        return 0
+    if num_decode_tokens <= int(qo_len.sum().item()):
+        return 0
+    if num_decode_tokens % num_reqs != 0:
+        return 0
+
+    uniform_qo_len = num_decode_tokens // num_reqs
+    if uniform_qo_len <= 1:
+        return 0
+
+    positive_qo_len = qo_len[qo_len > 0]
+    if positive_qo_len.numel() == qo_len.numel():
+        return 0
+    if positive_qo_len.numel() > 0:
+        if max_qo_len != uniform_qo_len:
+            return 0
+        if not torch.all(positive_qo_len == uniform_qo_len):
+            return 0
+
+    zero_positions = torch.nonzero(qo_len == 0, as_tuple=False).flatten()
+    if zero_positions.numel() > 0:
+        first_zero = int(zero_positions[0].item())
+        if torch.any(qo_len[first_zero:] > 0):
+            return 0
+
+    return uniform_qo_len
+
+
+_ACTUAL = AiterMLAMetadataBuilder._uniform_padded_mtp_qo_len
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_reqs", [1, 2, 3, 4])
+def test_matches_reference_exhaustively(num_reqs):
+    """Every qo_len vector x decode-token count x max_qo_len in a small space."""
+    checked = 0
+    for lens in itertools.product(range(0, 4), repeat=num_reqs):
+        qo = torch.tensor(lens, dtype=torch.int32)
+        for num_decode_tokens in range(0, 13):
+            for max_qo_len in range(0, 5):
+                got = _ACTUAL(qo, max_qo_len, num_decode_tokens)
+                want = _reference(qo, max_qo_len, num_decode_tokens)
+                assert got == want, (
+                    f"lens={lens} num_decode_tokens={num_decode_tokens} "
+                    f"max_qo_len={max_qo_len}: got {got}, reference {want}"
+                )
+                checked += 1
+    assert checked > 0
+
+
+def test_empty_batch():
+    assert _ACTUAL(torch.zeros(0, dtype=torch.int32), 4, 8) == 0
+    assert _reference(torch.zeros(0, dtype=torch.int32), 4, 8) == 0
+
+
+def test_the_padded_mtp_case_that_should_succeed():
+    """A live prefix at the uniform width, then zero-padded dummies."""
+    qo = torch.tensor([4, 4, 0, 0], dtype=torch.int32)
+    # 4 requests x 4 tokens = 16 captured, 8 live -> dummies are synthesizable.
+    assert _ACTUAL(qo, 4, 16) == 4
+    assert _reference(qo, 4, 16) == 4
+
+
+def test_positive_after_zero_is_rejected():
+    """A live request after a padding hole breaks the contiguous-prefix layout."""
+    qo = torch.tensor([4, 0, 4, 0], dtype=torch.int32)
+    assert _ACTUAL(qo, 4, 16) == 0
+    assert _reference(qo, 4, 16) == 0
+
+
+def test_ragged_live_lengths_are_rejected():
+    qo = torch.tensor([4, 2, 0, 0], dtype=torch.int32)
+    assert _ACTUAL(qo, 4, 16) == 0
+    assert _reference(qo, 4, 16) == 0

@@ -2548,16 +2548,26 @@ def build(
                     "Non-causal multi-token MLA requires an explicitly supported "
                     "attention group."
                 )
-            query_lens = query_start_loc_cpu[1:] - query_start_loc_cpu[:-1]
-            num_active_reqs = int(torch.count_nonzero(query_lens > 0))
-            uniform_active_queries = num_active_reqs > 0 and bool(
-                torch.all(query_lens[:num_active_reqs] == query_lens[0])
+            # query_start_loc_cpu is host-side and holds one entry per
+            # request, so this check costs more in tensor dispatch than in
+            # the work it does. Read it out once and validate on Python ints:
+            # the block runs on every build, between decode steps.
+            qsl = query_start_loc_cpu.tolist()
+            query_lens = [qsl[i + 1] - qsl[i] for i in range(len(qsl) - 1)]
+            num_active_reqs = 0
+            for qlen in query_lens:
+                if qlen > 0:
+                    num_active_reqs += 1
+            uniform_active_queries = num_active_reqs > 0 and all(
+                qlen == query_lens[0] for qlen in query_lens[:num_active_reqs]
+            )
+            trailing_graph_padding = all(
+                qlen == 0 for qlen in query_lens[num_active_reqs:]
             )
-            trailing_graph_padding = bool(torch.all(query_lens[num_active_reqs:] == 0))
             if not (uniform_active_queries and trailing_graph_padding):
                 raise ValueError(
                     "Non-causal MLA requires a uniform query block; got query "
-                    f"lengths {query_lens.tolist()}."
+                    f"lengths {query_lens}."
                 )
             # Use exact GPU sequence lengths instead of the prefill path's CPU
             # context-length upper bounds.

@@ -563,28 +563,41 @@ def _uniform_padded_mtp_qo_len(
         # query_start_loc flat for dummy requests. Only synthesize dummy rows
         # when every padded request maps to the same qlen and the q buffer has
         # exactly that many rows.
-        if num_decode_tokens <= int(qo_len.sum().item()):
-            return 0
         if num_decode_tokens % num_reqs != 0:
             return 0
 
         uniform_qo_len = num_decode_tokens // num_reqs
         if uniform_qo_len <= 1:
             return 0
 
-        positive_qo_len = qo_len[qo_len > 0]
-        if positive_qo_len.numel() == qo_len.numel():
+        # qo_len is derived from query_start_loc_cpu, so it is already
+        # host-side and tiny (one entry per request). Reading it out once and
+        # deciding on Python ints avoids eight separate tensor dispatches --
+        # sum/item, boolean-mask index, all, eq, nonzero, item, any -- on the
+        # metadata-build path, which runs between decode steps while the GPUs
+        # are idle.
+        lens = qo_len.tolist()
+        if num_decode_tokens <= sum(lens):
+            return 0
+
+        first_zero = -1
+        num_positive = 0
+        for i, qlen in enumerate(lens):
+            if qlen > 0:
+                num_positive += 1
+                # A positive entry after a zero breaks the contiguous live
+                # prefix that the padded layout requires.
+                if first_zero >= 0:
+                    return 0
+            elif first_zero < 0:
+                first_zero = i
+
+        if num_positive == num_reqs:
             return 0
-        if positive_qo_len.numel() > 0:
+        if num_positive > 0:
             if max_qo_len != uniform_qo_len:
                 return 0
-            if not torch.all(positive_qo_len == uniform_qo_len):
-                return 0
-
-        zero_positions = torch.nonzero(qo_len == 0, as_tuple=False).flatten()
-        if zero_positions.numel() > 0:
-            first_zero = int(zero_positions[0].item())
-            if torch.any(qo_len[first_zero:] > 0):
+            if any(qlen != uniform_qo_len for qlen in lens if qlen > 0):
                 return 0
 
         return uniform_qo_len

issue_comments.body:
Note in case anyone saw the earlier version of this PR: I briefly added two commits changing the MLA decode `kv_granularity` from 16 to 256, plus a section in the description. **Both have been reverted and the description restored.** This PR is back to being purely the bit-exact host-dispatch cleanup it started as.

Why I withdrew it: the change had already been evaluated and deliberately rejected in our own benchmark tree. It was defaulted to 512 on microbenchmark evidence, then reverted to 16 because end to end the two measured **within noise** at concurrency 1 — the +0.86% interactivity p90 never cleared the ~1% noise floor. The general point is worth restating, since it applies to a lot of kernel-level work on this path: MLA decode is only ~5-9% of the decode step, so even a 15-25% kernel-level improvement lands under 1% end to end.

My own sweep, which is what prompted the proposal, turned out to argue the same way once run at the right operating point: **+23.8% at ctx=65536 but only +1.58% at 384k**, the context the p90 request actually carries — roughly 0.22% of the decode step.

Sorry for the noise. Nothing in the current diff is affected.

[#13904](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13904) reports "passed and

**@LucasWilkinson @MatthewBonanni** — this PR touches
`vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py` (+16/-6), which you own
in CODEOWNERS, so it needs an approval from one of you. The change is confined
to the non-causal MLA query-block validation in `build()`: it reads
`query_start_loc_cpu` once via `.tolist()` and does the uniformity and
trailing-padding checks on Python ints, instead of `torch.count_nonzero` plus
two `torch.all` calls on a host tensor holding one entry per request. Same
accept/reject decision, same error message; it is host dispatch overhead on
the per-build path rather than a behaviour change. Equivalence is covered by
the sweep in `tests/v1/attention/test_aiter_mla_uniform_mtp_qo_len.py`.
